Subject: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Hi Emily —

Thanks again for taking the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have an aligned POC plan: 

Summary of our goals
- Validate Redwood Dedicated for AcmeHealth inference for clinical triage assistant (throughput + latency + cost).
- Primary success criteria: p95 latency <= 250ms for 95% of requests at target RPS; qualitative parity with current baseline prompts.

Evaluation plan (high level)
1) Baseline run with 1 week of representative traffic (we'll mirror sample requests).
2) Stress run to validate concurrency and burst handling (see questions below).
3) Cost & quality analysis vs. current deployed system.

What I need from your team to lock the POC scope:
- Workload profile: steady-state RPS, typical peak RPS, expected concurrency, token length distribution (avg/min/max), and burst patterns (time-of-day).
- Any protected-data considerations or network constraints for the trial environment.
- Primary contacts: who will provide test data and own acceptance criteria on your side?

Proposed timeline
- Week of Mar 22: Provisioning + kickoff
- Weeks of Mar 29–Apr 5: Baseline and stress runs
- Week of Apr 12: Wrap-up + review

Owners
- Redwood AE: Ben Carter (me) — commercial coordination
- Redwood CS: Marissa Cole — trial setup, ingestion, evaluation metrics
- Redwood SE: Dylan Brooks — environment, test harness, load generation
- AcmeHealth: please confirm a primary and backup owner

Attachments: I can share a sample intake spreadsheet to make it easy to fill in.

If that looks right, can you send the workload numbers this week? Happy to take a quick 15-min call to walk through the intake sheet.

Best,
Ben
Ben Carter

Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Thanks Ben — good recap. See answers below and attached a draft workload intake spreadsheet.

Workload profile (prod baseline, representative for POC)
- Steady-state RPS: ~1.5 requests/sec (mostly daytime)
- Typical peak RPS: 12–25 requests/sec (weekly spikes during 09:00–11:00 and 15:00–16:00 PT)
- Concurrency (simultaneous active requests we expect): 8–20, depending on customer activity windows
- Token lengths: min ~20, avg ~120, median ~95, max ~350 (we have longer summary requests occasionally)
- Burst patterns: 5–10 minute bursts up to 60 requests (rare), most common short spikes ~20–30 seconds during chart refreshes

Other notes
- Test data: Rajesh will provide a sanitized sample set (no PHI) and a small set with hashed identifiers for quality checks.
- Network: we prefer VPC peering for the Dedicated trial; will confirm firewall rules for outbound to Redwood.

Attachments: acme_workload_profile.xlsx [Attachment: acme_workload_profile.xlsx (Excel, 48KB)]

Let us know if you want these numbers in a different format. Primary owner on our side for the POC will be Rajesh Singh (cc'd).

Best,
Emily Chen
Director of Platform Engineering, AcmeHealth
emily.chen@acmehealth.com

Subject: Re: POC trial planning & workload intake — AcmeHealth

Emily — thanks for the fast turnaround and the attachment. This is exactly what we need. A few follow-ups and proposed acceptance criteria so we can sign off quickly: 

POC acceptance criteria (proposed)
- Latency: p95 generation latency <= 250ms for requests <= 200 tokens; p95 <= 600ms for requests up to 350 tokens
- Throughput: handle sustained 25 RPS with p95 latency under the targets above for 90% of the test window
- Quality: human evaluation > 90% of sampled responses meeting your checklist (Rajesh to provide checklist)
- Cost: projected per-1M-token cost target to be shared after initial baseline run

Test plan highlights
- Baseline: replay ~24 hours of sampled traffic from your sanitized data set
- Stress: run 3 x 30-minute sustained bursts at 25 RPS, plus a 10-minute extreme burst test up to 60 RPS to validate graceful degradation
- Monitoring: capture p50/p95/p99 latencies, token counts, failure rate, and cost breakdown per 1k requests

Action items
- Redwood: prepare Dedicated trial environment (VPC peering), provide test harness and load scripts — owner Dylan
- AcmeHealth: provide sanitized sample data + evaluation checklist — owner Rajesh
- Schedule: kickoff the week of Mar 22; recommend Tues Mar 23 10:00 PT for a 30-min kickoff (open to reschedule)

Links
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME-2314
- Intake folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcDeFgHjkLmNoPqR

If that looks good, we'll open the provisioning ticket and lock the kickoff.

Cheers,
Ben
